Follow the documented defaults and keep moving unless the guide requires a project-specific decision, the change is destructive, credentials or environment setup are missing, or the correct migration is ambiguous. Keep the migration scoped to the upgrade, inspect the diff, run the relevant checks, and fix remaining breaking changes.
00023| 
00024| After the app is upgraded, use the runtime verification flow from the [AI Coding Agents guide](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents) to confirm it still works. Prefer the `next-dev-loop` skill when it is available (Next.js 16.3 or later with Turbopack); otherwise fall back to the best available `next dev`, browser, and build checks. Open the key interactive UI states and check the Next dev indicator plus browser and server logs. Summarize what changed, what was verified, and what could not be verified.
00025| 
00026| Before finishing, repeat the post-upgrade check in [Set up AI agent docs](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#set-up-ai-agent-docs) so the project is ready for future agent work.
00027| ```
00028| 
00029| ## Or upgrade manually
00030| 
00031| Upgrading manually follows a few steps, in order:
00032| 
00033| 1. [Set up AI agent docs](#set-up-ai-agent-docs) if you use an assistant now or want future agent work grounded in version-matched docs.
00034| 2. [Run the upgrade codemod](#using-the-codemod).
00035| 3. If you prefer not to run the codemod, [install packages manually](#install-packages-manually).
00036| 4. Continue through the breaking changes below, run the relevant checks, and fix any remaining issues.
00037| 
00038| ## Set up AI agent docs
00039| 
00040| The prompt above asks the agent to do this before it edits code. You can also prepare the project yourself before starting the upgrade. See the [AI Coding Agents guide](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents) for the full setup.
00041| 
00042| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00043| npx @next/codemod@canary agents-md
00044| ```
00045| 
00046| After upgrading, verify `AGENTS.md` still points at the docs for the installed Next.js version. On Next.js 16.2 and later, that should be the bundled docs in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/`. If the pre-upgrade setup downloaded docs into `.next-docs/`, update `AGENTS.md` to point at the bundled docs, then remove `.next-docs/` once nothing references it.
00047| 
00048| The managed block should look like this:
00049| 
00050| ```md filename="AGENTS.md"
00051| <!-- BEGIN:nextjs-agent-rules -->
00052| 
00053| # This is NOT the Next.js you know
00054| 
00055| This version has breaking changes — APIs, conventions, and file structure may all differ from your training data. Read the relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` (resolved from this file's directory; in monorepos the `next` package may not be visible from the repo root) before writing any code. Heed deprecation notices.
00056| 
00057| This block is written and re-added by `next dev` — verify at `node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/generate-agent-files.js`. Removing it from a diff only re-creates the uncommitted change; committing it with your work keeps the tree clean.
00058| 
00059| <!-- END:nextjs-agent-rules -->
00060| ```
00061| 
00062| ## Using the codemod
00063| 
00064| To update to Next.js version 16, you can use the `upgrade` [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#160):
00065| 
00066| ```bash package="pnpm"
00067| pnpm dlx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest
00068| ```
00069| 
00070| ```bash package="npm"
00071| npx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest
00072| ```
00073| 
00074| ```bash package="yarn"
00075| yarn dlx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest
00076| ```
00077| 
00078| ```bash package="bun"
00079| bunx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest
00080| ```
00081| 
00082| The [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#160) is able to:
00083| 
00084| - Update `next.config.js` to use the new `turbopack` configuration
00085| - Migrate from `next lint` to the ESLint CLI
00086| - Migrate from deprecated `middleware` convention to `proxy`
00087| - Remove `unstable_` prefix from stabilized APIs
00088| - Remove `experimental_ppr` Route Segment Config from pages and layouts
00089| 
00090| The `upgrade` codemod does not run every migration codemod. If your app still uses synchronous `params`, `searchParams`, `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `draftMode()` access from the Next.js 15 compatibility period, also run the async Request APIs codemod:
00091| 
00092| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00093| npx @next/codemod@canary next-async-request-api .
00094| ```
00095| 
00096| ## Install packages manually
00097| 
00098| If you prefer to do it manually, install the latest Next.js and React versions:
00099| 
00100| ```bash package="pnpm"
00101| pnpm add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest
00102| ```
00103| 
00104| ```bash package="npm"
00105| npm install next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest
00106| ```
00107| 
00108| ```bash package="yarn"
00109| yarn add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest
00110| ```
00111| 
00112| ```bash package="bun"
00113| bun add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest
00114| ```
00115| 
00116| If you are using TypeScript, ensure you also upgrade `@types/react` and `@types/react-dom` to their latest versions.
00117| 
00118| ## Node.js runtime and browser support
00119| 
00120| | Requirement   | Change / Details                                                   |
00121| | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
00122| | Node.js 20.9+ | Minimum version now `20.9.0` (LTS); Node.js 18 no longer supported |
00123| | TypeScript 5+ | Minimum version now `5.1.0`                                        |
00124| | Browsers      | Chrome 111+, Edge 111+, Firefox 111+, Safari 16.4+                 |
00125| 
00126| ## Turbopack by default
00127| 
00128| Starting with **Next.js 16**, Turbopack is stable and used by default with `next dev` and `next build`
00129| 
00130| Previously you had to enable Turbopack using `--turbopack`, or `--turbo`.
00131| 
00132| ```json filename="package.json"
00133| {
00134|   "scripts": {
00135|     "dev": "next dev --turbopack",
00136|     "build": "next build --turbopack",
00137|     "start": "next start"
00138|   }
00139| }
00140| ```
00141| 
00142| This is no longer necessary. You can update your `package.json` scripts:
00143| 
00144| ```json filename="package.json"
00145| {
00146|   "scripts": {
00147|     "dev": "next dev",
00148|     "build": "next build",
00149|     "start": "next start"
00150|   }
00151| }
00152| ```
00153| 
00154| If your project has a [custom `webpack`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/webpack) configuration and you run `next build` (which now uses Turbopack by default), the build will **fail** to prevent misconfiguration issues.
00155| 
00156| You have a few different ways to address this:
00157| 
00158| - **Use Turbopack anyway:** Run with `next build --turbopack` to build using Turbopack and ignore your `webpack` config.
00159| - **Switch to Turbopack fully:** Migrate your `webpack` config to Turbopack-compatible options.
00160| - **Keep using Webpack:** Use the `--webpack` flag to opt out of Turbopack and build with Webpack.
00161| 
00162| > **Good to know**: If you see failing builds because a `webpack` configuration was found, but you don't define one yourself, it is likely that a plugin is adding a `webpack` option
00163| 
00164| ### Opting out of Turbopack
00165| 
00166| If you need to continue using Webpack, you can opt out with the `--webpack` flag. For example, to use Turbopack in development but Webpack for production builds:
00167| 
00168| ```json filename="package.json"
00169| {
00170|   "scripts": {
00171|     "dev": "next dev",
00172|     "build": "next build --webpack",
00173|     "start": "next start"
00174|   }
00175| }
00176| ```
00177| 
00178| We recommend using Turbopack for development and production. Submit a comment to this [thread](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/77721), if you are unable to switch to Turbopack.
00179| 
00180| ### Turbopack configuration location
00181| 
00182| The `experimental.turbopack` configuration is out of experimental.
00183| 
00184| ```ts filename="next.config.ts"

00195|

00197| ```

00015| // Return a list of `params` to populate the [slug] dynamic segment
00016| export async function generateStaticParams() {

00030| }) {

Next.js provides two conventions to handle not found cases:

- **`not-found.js`**: Used when you call the [`notFound`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) function in a route segment.
- **`global-not-found.js`**: Used to define a global 404 page for unmatched routes across your entire app. This is handled at the routing level and doesn't depend on rendering a layout or page.

## `not-found.js`

The **not-found** file is used to render UI when the [`notFound`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) function is thrown within a route segment. Errors can be divided into two categories: [expected errors](#handling-expected-errors) and [uncaught exceptions](#handling-uncaught-exceptions). This page will walk you through how you can handle these errors in your Next.js application.

## Handling expected errors

Expected errors are those that can occur during the normal operation of the application, such as those from [server-side form validation](/docs/app/guides/forms) or failed requests. These errors should be handled explicitly and returned to the client.

## Handling expected errors

Expected errors are those that can occur during the normal operation of the application, such as those from [server-side form validation](/docs/app/guides/forms) or failed requests. These errors should be handled explicitly and returned to the client.

00013| ## Route Handlers
00014| 
00015| Route Handlers allow you to create custom request handlers for a given route using the Web [Request](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request) and [Response](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Response) APIs.
00016| 
00017| <Image
00018|   alt="Route.js Special File"
00019|   srcLight="/docs/light/route-special-file.png"
00020|   srcDark="/docs/dark/route-special-file.png"
00021|   width="1600"
00022|   height="444"
00023| />
00024| 
00025| > **Good to know**: Route Handlers are only available inside the `app` directory. They are the equivalent of [API Routes](/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing/api-routes) inside the `pages` directory meaning you **do not** need to use API Routes and Route Handlers together.
00026| 
00027| ### Convention
00028| 
00029| Route Handlers are defined in a [`route.js|ts` file](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) inside the `app` directory:
00030| 
00031| ```ts filename="app/api/route.ts" switcher
00032| export async function GET(request: Request) {}
00033| ```
00034| 
00035| ```js filename="app/api/route.js" switcher
00036| export async function GET(request) {}
00037| ```
00038| 
00039| Route Handlers can be nested anywhere inside the `app` directory, similar to `page.js` and `layout.js`. But there **cannot** be a `route.js` file at the same route segment level as `page.js`.
00040| 
00041| ### Supported HTTP Methods
00042| 
00043| The following [HTTP methods](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods) are supported: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `HEAD`, and `OPTIONS`. If an unsupported method is called, Next.js will return a `405 Method Not Allowed` response.
00044| 
00045| ### Extended `NextRequest` and `NextResponse` APIs
00046| 
00047| In addition to supporting the native [Request](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request) and [Response](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Response) APIs, Next.js extends them with [`NextRequest`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-request) and [`NextResponse`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-response) to provide convenient helpers for advanced use cases.
00048| 
00049| ### Caching
00050| 
00051| Route Handlers are not cached by default. You can, however, opt into caching for `GET` methods. Other supported HTTP methods are **not** cached. To cache a `GET` method, use a [route config option](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic) such as `export const dynamic = 'force-static'` in your Route Handler file.
00052| 
00053| ```ts filename="app/items/route.ts" switcher
00054| export const dynamic = 'force-static'
00055| 
00056| export async function GET() {
00057|   const res = await fetch('https://data.mongodb-api.com/...', {
00058|     headers: {
00059|       'Content-Type': 'application/json',
00060|       'API-Key': process.env.DATA_API_KEY,
00061|     },
00062|   })
00063|   const data = await res.json()
00064| 
00065|   return Response.json({ data })
00066| }
00067| ```
00068| 
00069| ```js filename="app/items/route.js" switcher
00070| export const dynamic = 'force-static'
00071| 
00072| export async function GET() {
00073|   const res = await fetch('https://data.mongodb-api.com/...', {
00074|     headers: {
00075|       'Content-Type': 'application/json',
00076|       'API-Key': process.env.DATA_API_KEY,
00077|     },
00078|   })
00079|   const data = await res.json()
00080| 
00081|   return Response.json({ data })
00082| }
00083| ```
00084| 
00085| > **Good to know**: Other supported HTTP methods are **not** cached, even if they are placed alongside a `GET` method that is cached, in the same file.
00086| 
00087| #### With Cache Components
00088| 
00089| When [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) is enabled, `GET` Route Handlers follow the same model as normal UI routes in your application. They run at request time by default, can be prerendered when they don't access uncached or runtime data, and you can use `use cache` to include uncached data in the static response.
00090| 
00091| **Static example** - doesn't access uncached or runtime data, so it will be prerendered at build time:
00092| 
00093| ```tsx filename="app/api/project-info/route.ts"
00094| export async function GET() {
00095|   return Response.json({
00096|     projectName: 'Next.js',
00097|   })
00098| }
00099| ```
00100|

00013| ## Route Handlers
00014| 
00015| Route Handlers allow you to create custom request handlers for a given route using the Web [Request](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request) and [Response](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Response) APIs.
00016| 
00017| <Image
00018|   alt="Route.js Special File"
00019|   srcLight="/docs/light/route-special-file.png"
00020|   srcDark="/docs/dark/route-special-file.png"
00021|   width="1600"
00022|   height="444"
00023| />
00024| 
00025| > **Good to know**: Route Handlers are only available inside the `app` directory. They are the equivalent of [API Routes](/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing/api-routes) inside the `pages` directory meaning you **do not** need to use API Routes and Route Handlers together.
00026| 
00027| ### Convention
00028| 
00029| Route Handlers are defined in a [`route.js|ts` file](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) inside the `app` directory:
00030| 
00031| ```ts filename="app/api/route.ts" switcher
00032| export async function GET(request: Request) {}
00033| ```
00034| 
00035| ```js filename="app/api/route.js" switcher
00036| export async function GET(request) {}
00037| ```
00038| 
00039| Route Handlers can be nested anywhere inside the `app` directory, similar to `page.js` and `layout.js`. But there **cannot** be a `route.js` file at the same route segment level as `page.js`.
00040| 
00041| ### Supported HTTP Methods
00042| 
00043| The following [HTTP methods](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods) are supported: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `HEAD`, and `OPTIONS`. If an unsupported method is called, Next.js will return a `405 Method Not Allowed` response.
00044| 
00045| ### Extended `NextRequest` and `NextResponse` APIs
00046| 
00047| In addition to supporting the native [Request](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request) and [Response](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Response) APIs, Next.js extends them with [`NextRequest`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-request) and [`NextResponse`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-response) to provide convenient helpers for advanced use cases.
00048| 
00049| ### Caching
00050| 
00051| Route Handlers are not cached by default. You can, however, opt into caching for `GET` methods. Other supported HTTP methods are **not** cached. To cache a `GET` method, use a [route config option](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic) such as `export const dynamic = 'force-static'` in your Route Handler file.
00052| 
00053| ```ts filename="app/items/route.ts" switcher
00054| export const dynamic = 'force-static'
00055| 
00056| export async function GET() {
00057|   const res = await fetch('https://data.mongodb-api.com/...', {
00058|     headers: {
00059|       'Content-Type': 'application/json',
00060|       'API-Key': process.env.DATA_API_KEY,
00061|     },
00062|   })
00063|   const data = await res.json()
00064| 
00065|   return Response.json({ data })
00066| }
00067| ```
00068| 
00069| ```js filename="app/items/route.js" switcher
00070| export const dynamic = 'force-static'
00071| 
00072| export async function GET() {
00073|   const res = await fetch('https://data.mongodb-api.com/...', {
00074|     headers: {
00075|       'Content-Type': 'application/json',
00076|       'API-Key': process.env.DATA_API_KEY,
00077|     },
00078|   })
00079|   const data = await res.json()
00080| 
00081|   return Response.json({ data })
00082| }
00083| ```
00084| 
00085| > **Good to know**: Other supported HTTP methods are **not** cached, even if they are placed alongside a `GET` method that is cached, in the same file.
00086| 
00087| #### With Cache Components
00088| 
00089| When [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) is enabled, `GET` Route Handlers follow the same model as normal UI routes in your application. They run at request time by default, can be prerendered when they don't access uncached or runtime data, and you can use `use cache` to include uncached data in the static response.
00090| 
00091| **Static example** - doesn't access uncached or runtime data, so it will be prerendered at build time:
00092| 
00093| ```tsx filename="app/api/project-info/route.ts"
00094| export async function GET() {
00095|   return Response.json({
00096|     projectName: 'Next.js',
00097|   })
00098| }
00099| ```
00100|

[`next/font`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/font) automatically optimizes your fonts (including custom fonts) and removes external network requests for improved privacy and performance.

It includes **built-in automatic self-hosting** for any font file. This means you can optimally load web fonts with no [layout shift](https://web.dev/articles/cls).

You can also conveniently use all [Google Fonts](https://fonts.google.com/). CSS and font files are downloaded at build time and self-hosted with the rest of your static assets. **No requests are sent to Google by the browser.**

<AppOnly>

```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher

  const pageSegments = normalize(pagePath).split(sep).filter(Boolean)

All routes and files have been migrated from the Pages Router to the App Router with TypeScript types, and the `pages/` directory has been removed.

### Key Changes
- **Root Layout & Global Setup (`app/layout.tsx`)**: Replaced `pages/_document.js` and `pages/_app.js` using Next.js `Metadata` API, `next/font/google` (`Inter`), and wrapping with the typed client context provider (`AppProvider`).
- **Context Provider (`components/AppProvider.tsx`)**: Converted `components/AppProvider.js` to TypeScript with `'use client'`, typing `theme` and `setTheme`.
- **Home Route (`app/page.tsx`, `app/home-page.tsx`)**: Replaced `getServerSideProps` with an async Server Component reading `headers()` from `next/headers` and fetching with `{ cache: 'no-store' }`. Extracted interactive client UI using `useRouter` from `next/navigation`.
- **Blog Index (`app/blog/page.tsx`, `app/blog/blog-list.tsx`)**: Replaced `getStaticProps` ISR (`revalidate: 60`) with an async Server Component with `revalidate = 60` and `next: { revalidate: 60 }`, coupled with a client component utilizing `useRouter` from `next/navigation`.
- **Blog Post (`app/blog/[id]/page.tsx`, `app/blog/[id]/blog-post.tsx`, `app/blog/[id]/loading.tsx`)**:
  - Replaced `getStaticPaths` with `generateStaticParams()` and `export const dynamicParams = true`.
  - Replaced `notFound: true` in `getStaticProps` with `notFound()` from `next/navigation`.
  - Replaced `router.isFallback` with `loading.tsx`.
  - Replaced `Head` with async `generateMetadata` consuming promise-based `params`.
  - Updated client actions to use `router.back()` from `next/navigation`.
- **API Routes (`app/api/posts/route.ts`, `app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts`)**: Migrated API routes to Route Handlers exporting standard HTTP methods (`GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`) with `NextResponse.json` and typed asynchronous route context parameters.
- **Error & 404 Handling (`app/not-found.tsx`, `app/error.tsx`, `app/global-error.tsx`)**: Replaced `pages/404.js` with `app/not-found.tsx` and `pages/_error.js` with client error boundaries `app/error.tsx` and `app/global-error.tsx`.
- **Pages Directory**: Completely removed `pages/`.
